key_insight: A steady, spatially varying Kolmogorov flow can drive a passive nematic from stationary to periodic and irregular dynamics without velocity fluctuations or hydrodynamic feedback.
engineering_relevance: The findings suggest that steady spatial shear could control time-dependent nematic responses without requiring time-varying forcing.
method: Study a planar passive nematic under prescribed steady Kolmogorov flow as flow strength increases.
Use bifurcation and phase-space analyses to characterize dynamical transitions.
Develop two-mode and five-mode reduced-order models to identify the underlying mechanisms.
evidence_signal: The two-mode model captures periodic onset through a saddle-node infinite-period bifurcation, while the five-mode Galerkin model reproduces the stationary-to-periodic-to-irregular progression.
watch_item: Velocity fluctuations and hydrodynamic feedback are excluded, so applicability to fully coupled nematic flows requires further validation.
paper_title: Complex nematic dynamics driven by steady Kolmogorov flows
